  "report_markdown": "# Yundera/AppStore — Dufs\n\n**Audit date:** 2026-08-19 · **Store version:** `sigoden/dufs:v0.45.0` · **Compose sha:** `2ae62e846ffa52416186f1dad41dec24b849ce18` (last touched by `0f5955e`, 2026-07-10)\n\n**Verdict: NON-COMPLIANT · Major** — risk score **12** (0 Critical · 1 Major · 2 Minor)\n\nScope: `Apps/Dufs/docker-compose.yml` @ `main`. Depth `static`; no `compose_base`, so scope detection is `n-a`. No `rationale.md` in the app directory (HTTP 404).\n\n---\n\n## Summary\n\nDufs is a well-formed store app in most respects: the image is pinned, authentication is genuinely enforced by default, the Caddy wiring is textbook, every asset resolves against `Yundera/AppStore@main`, and the app is stateless so there is nothing to lose on reinstall. It fails on one substantive item and two hygiene items.\n\nThe Major finding is that the compose binds the **entire `/DATA` root** into a read/write file server without the `rationale.md` that CONTRIBUTING.md requires for exactly that deviation. There is no Critical finding — in particular the `--enable-cors` flag, which looked like a candidate, was traced through upstream source and does not yield an exploitable cross-origin path.\n\n---\n\n## Tech & Documentation (static)\n\n### Failing items\n\n**1. `data-under-datadir` — FAIL · Major**\n\n```yaml\nvolumes:\n  - type: bind\n    source: /DATA\n    target: /srv\n```\n\nThe whole `/DATA` root is served with `--allow-upload --allow-delete --allow-symlink --allow-archive` behind a single `admin` account. This is strictly broader than the union of `/DATA/AppData/Dufs/` and the four user directories, because it also exposes `/DATA/AppData/<every-other-app>/` — other apps' configs, databases and stored secrets — as readable, writable and deletable through the web UI and WebDAV.\n\nCONTRIBUTING.md requires a `rationale.md` whenever an app \"exposes volumes outside `/DATA/AppData/[AppName]/` and `/DATA/[user-dir]/`\". `Apps/Dufs/rationale.md` returns 404.\n\n*Weighing context for the reviewer:* sibling **FileBrowser** ships the same `/DATA/` → `/srv/` mount and also has no `rationale.md`, so there is store precedent for this app class. The distinction is that FileBrowser mediates access through its own per-user ACL database, whereas Dufs grants blanket rw+delete over the entire tree to one credential. If the store intends to bless this pattern for file servers, the clean fix is a short `rationale.md` here (and on FileBrowser) rather than silent precedent.\n\n**2. `cpu-shares` — FAIL · Minor**\n\nNo `cpu_shares` field on the service. The compose sets `deploy.resources.limits.cpus: '0.5'` and `memory: 128M` instead — CONTRIBUTING.md explicitly distinguishes these (\"`cpu_shares` is a **top-level service field**, not part of `deploy:`\"); a hard CPU cap is not a relative share. Every comparable shipped app sets it: FileBrowser `10`, Nextcloud `70`, Seafile `80/70/30`. Expected tier for a user-facing file server is **50**.\n\n**3. `volume-env-descriptions` — FAIL · Minor**\n\nThe single bind mount carries no description, no inline comment, and no mention in the description or `tips`; `PUID`/`PGID`/`TZ` are likewise undescribed. This compounds finding 1: nothing anywhere in the app text tells the user that installing Dufs publishes their entire `/DATA` tree over the web. Nextcloud annotates each of its volumes; Dufs annotates none.\n\n### Passing items\n\n| Item | Verdict | Evidence |\n|---|---|---|\n| `pinned-image-tag` | pass | `sigoden/dufs:v0.45.0`; no other images referenced |\n| `permissions` | pass | Rule **D4** — `user: $PUID:$PGID`, PUID/PGID/TZ exported, all mounts within `/DATA`. Not root; no `privileged`/`cap_add`, so D1/D2/D3/D5 do not apply |\n| `auth-default` | pass | `--auth admin:$APP_DEFAULT_PASSWORD@/:rw`. Verified in dufs v0.45.0 `src/auth.rs`: one non-empty account rule leaves `anonymous = None`, so `guard()` returns `(None, None)` and denies every unauthenticated non-OPTIONS request. Documented in `tips.before_install` (en_us + zh_cn) |\n| `no-hardcoded-credentials` | pass | Only credential is the injected `$APP_DEFAULT_PASSWORD`; `admin` is a disclosed non-secret default |\n| `state-persistence` | pass | dufs is stateless — config is CLI flags only, the ACL is parsed from `--auth` at boot, and there is no database, index or cache on disk (`--allow-search` walks the FS live). No app state location exists to map, so nothing is lost on uninstall/reinstall |\n| `install-cmd-security` | n-a | Neither `pre-install-cmd` nor `post-install-cmd` is declared |\n| `assets` | pass | All five files present; all five jsDelivr URLs return 200 against `Yundera/AppStore@main`. icon 192×192, thumbnail 784×442, thumbnail distinct from screenshot-1 (different md5) |\n| `name-regex` | pass | `name: dufs` matches `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]*$` |\n| `container-name` | pass | `container_name: dufs` == `name:` == service key; stable for Caddy container-DNS |\n| `caddy-wiring` | pass | `expose: 80`; caddy_0/1/2 → `{{upstreams 80}}`; `gateway_tls` on 0 and 1 but correctly not on 2; `pcs` external; no `auth-${APP_DOMAIN}` collision |\n| `casaos-coherence` | pass | `main: dufs` resolves to the labelled service; `webui_port: 80` == `expose` == `--port 80`; `index: /` valid (no AUTH_HASH) |\n| `architectures` | pass | Declares amd64/arm64/arm; Docker Hub manifest list for `v0.45.0` publishes linux/amd64, linux/arm64, linux/386, linux/armv7 |\n| `description` | pass | Detailed `en_us` plus `zh_cn`; title and tagline in both. Mandatory en_us satisfied |\n\n---\n\n## Security / tech opinions (advisory — not scored)\n\n- **`--enable-cors` (medium confidence, investigated and cleared).** `add_cors()` in `src/server.rs` emits `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`, `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true`, `Allow-Methods: *` and `Allow-Headers: Authorization,*`. This was assessed as a Critical candidate and rejected: per the Fetch spec a browser rejects any `credentials: include` request whose ACAO is the wildcard, so the drive-by CSRF read against a logged-in user is blocked, and a non-credentialed cross-origin request is denied 401 by `guard()`. Residual concern only — the wildcard plus `Allow-Headers: Authorization` invites any origin to drive the API once it holds the password, and the flag buys nothing for the documented web-UI and WebDAV use cases. Dropping it is free hardening.\n- **`--allow-symlink` (low confidence).** Permits following symlinks out of the served root. Symlinks cannot be created over HTTP/WebDAV, and resolution happens inside the container's namespace as a non-root user, so impact is limited to the app's own minimal image — but the flag is unnecessary for the advertised feature set.\n- **`--auth` string fragility (low confidence).** `split_account_paths` splits on the first `@/` and `split_once(':')` on the first `:`, so a generated password containing `:`, `@` or `|` parses correctly; only a literal `@/` inside `$APP_DEFAULT_PASSWORD` would mis-parse. An empty password fails closed (container refuses to start). No action required.\n- **Screenshot dimensions (note).** `screenshot-1.png` is 755×272, below the 1280×720 *featured-app* guideline. Not a baseline requirement, so not scored.\n\n---\n\n## Functionality\n\n**Not run — depth = `static`.** Phases A, C, D, E8, E9, E10, F and G were not executed and no functional phase results were recorded. Per the 2026-07-07 amendment, a static-only audit can never on its own establish `compliant`; this verdict rests on the static checklist failures above, which are conclusive regardless of functional outcome.\n\n---\n\n## Gate application\n\n1. No finding carries `severity = Critical` → gate rule B1 not triggered.\n2. Three `fail` items exist (1 Major, 2 Minor) → **rule B2: NON-COMPLIANT**.\n3. Risk score = 100·0 + 10·1 + 1·2 = **12** (triage only; does not affect the verdict).\n\n## Recommended remediation\n\n1. Add `Apps/Dufs/rationale.md` documenting the whole-`/DATA` mount — why the full tree rather than the user directories, what the single-account rw+delete exposure means for other apps' AppData, and what mitigations apply. *(clears the Major)*\n2. Add `cpu_shares: 50` as a top-level field on the `dufs` service, keeping the existing `deploy.resources.limits`. *(clears a Minor)*\n3. Comment the `/DATA` → `/srv` mount and add a line to `tips.before_install` stating that Dufs exposes the entire `/DATA` tree. *(clears a Minor, and is the highest-value change for users)*\n4. Optional hardening: drop `--enable-cors` and `--allow-symlink` unless a consumer needs them.\n"
